name: Tool Graph Retriever (TGR)
venue: arXiv 2508.05152 (cs.IR; preprint, no peer-reviewed venue confirmed)
authors_affiliation: Linfeng Gao, Yaoxiang Wang, Yuzhe Shang, Jinsong Su (School of Informatics, Xiamen University, China); Minlong Peng, Mingming Sun (Baidu, Beijing, China); Jialong Tang (Alibaba). Corresponding/lead: Linfeng Gao and Jinsong Su (Xiamen University).
code_url: [uncertain] No official code repository linked in the paper or found via search; the paper introduces dataset TDI300K but no public release URL is given.
task_domain: tool-use (tool retrieval for LLM agents): retrieving relevant tools/APIs from a large tool set so an LLM can plan and invoke them.
problem_setting: Offline-trained, single-agent tool retrieval for LLM agents. Given a user query and a large equipped tool/API set, retrieve the relevant tools (including non-obvious prerequisite tools) before the LLM plans and invokes them. Supervision is available: a BERT discriminator is trained on the constructed TDI300K dataset (pretraining on LLM-generated CodeSearchNet-derived pairs + finetuning on manually annotated pairs) to identify pairwise tool dependencies; the retriever itself reuses off-the-shelf / previously-finetuned text embedding models (PMLM-L3-v2, ToolBench-IR) augmented with a parameter-free graph convolution over the tool dependency graph. Retrieval is a one-shot, task-level ranking step; the LLM planning/invocation loop is downstream and not the contribution.
what_is_retrieved: tools / APIs (tool documents containing name, description, parameters for ToolBench; tool descriptions for API-Bank).
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus (a fixed candidate tool/API set indexed offline). The tool dependency graph and tool embeddings are induced offline and frozen; no growing/episodic agent-written memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Completeness-oriented within a top-k framing: the core motivation is recovering the complete minimal set of needed tools including prerequisite tools that have low semantic similarity to the query. Evaluated via Pass Rate@k (pass@k = fraction of queries whose ALL ground-truth tools fall within top-k), alongside Recall@k and NDCG@k. k is fixed (top-5, top-10).
explicit_cbr_grounding: false; the work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It is dependency-graph-based tool retrieval.
retrieval_unit: tool-API. Each node is a single tool/API represented by its tool document/description embedding.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced. Candidate tools are encoded offline; a tool dependency graph is constructed offline via a trained discriminator; graph convolution updates embeddings offline; the resulting tool representations are used for online query-time retrieval but the store is frozen (not grown at test time).
index_structure_topology: Dependency GRAPH: tools are nodes, identified pairwise dependencies are edges. For ToolBench, APIs are first grouped by category and a separate dependency graph is built within each category group; for API-Bank a single graph over the tool set is built. (Connected-node proportion: 0.420 for API-Bank, 0.824 for ToolBench.)
retriever_type: dense (text-embedding based) retriever augmented with graph convolution. Base retrievers are dense text embedding models (Paraphrase MiniLM-L3-v2, ToolBench-IR); TGR refines their tool embeddings via GCN over the dependency graph. Word-frequency baselines (BM25, TF-IDF) are compared but not the proposed retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: Two-part: (a) the dependency discriminator is trained with supervised contrastive/classification signal (3-class cross-entropy: a->b, no-dependency, a<-b) on similarity-style dependency labels, via 2-stage pretraining (LLM-generated balanced data) + finetuning (manually annotated imbalanced data with a category-specific average loss); (b) the retriever embeddings come from off-the-shelf or previously-task-finetuned encoders, and the graph convolution itself is PARAMETER-FREE (GCN trainable weights removed for efficiency). So TGR adds no new retriever-training signal beyond the dependency discriminator; it propagates dependency structure into embeddings without learning retrieval weights.
query_construction: Raw user query encoded into an embedding by the base text encoder; no decomposition, expansion, or thought-conditioning. Query-tool similarity over the dependency-updated tool embeddings yields the retrieval score.
query_granularity: task-level (one-shot at t=0): a single query embedding is matched against the candidate tool set per task.
when_to_retrieve: one-shot (single retrieval pass per query, returning top-k tools before LLM planning).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule (retrieve once per query at the start). No confidence/uncertainty/learned-router trigger.
reranking: No separate learned reranking stage in the conventional sense. The dependency-aware effect is realized via graph convolution that updates tool embeddings before similarity ranking (i.e., dependency information is injected into representations, then a single descending similarity ranking is applied). This functions as a dependency-aware representation update rather than a post-hoc cross-encoder reranker.
retrieved_context_refinement: none (retrieved tools are returned as a top-k list; no decompose/distill/compress/distractor-filtering step on the retrieved set). The refinement happens at the index/representation level (GCN over dependencies), not on the retrieved context.
tool_document_engineering: Tool descriptions/documents are embedded by the base encoder: for ToolBench a structured document format (name, description, parameters) is used following Qin et al. (ToolBench); for API-Bank only the tool description is encoded (to mitigate query/tool-document domain mismatch). The key engineering is structural: dependency edges are added via a discriminator and folded into embeddings through graph convolution (not synthetic-query augmentation or weighted-field embeddings).
index_content_separation: N/A (no progressive-disclosure / lightweight-index-then-content separation; tool embeddings are computed directly).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Static tool index (offline-constructed dependency graph and embeddings). Tools/APIs originate from ToolBench (RapidAPI-derived) and API-Bank; no live MCP/RapidAPI auto-sync or CRUD synchronization is implemented. Graph construction is O(N^2), noted as a scalability limitation.
tool_dependency_awareness: Yes -- this is the central contribution. Inter-tool dependencies are explicitly modeled: tool a depends on tool b if (1) a needs b's output as input, or (2) a needs b for prior verification (e.g., UpdateInfo depends on Login depends on Validate). A trained 3-class discriminator identifies directed pairwise dependencies, forming a tool dependency graph; graph convolution (parameter-free GCN, Kipf & Welling 2017) propagates dependency information so prerequisite tools with low query similarity get retrieved.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the retrieved top-k tools are provided to the LLM so it can build a tool-invoking plan and execute tool calls. TGR's own contribution stops at producing the top-k retrieval list; the downstream agent loop (plan -> invoke -> feedback -> respond) is standard and not modified.
planning_integration: retrieve-then-plan: a one-shot tool retrieval precedes LLM planning. The retrieved tools (now including prerequisite tools surfaced via dependency-aware retrieval) are passed to the LLM, which then creates and executes a tool-invoking plan. No interleaving with search/MCTS.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer (retrieval is a single up-front step per query; not interleaved per reasoning step or per tool-call).
retrieved_item_representation: Raw tool documents/descriptions (tool name, description, parameters) returned as a ranked list of tools/APIs for prompt injection; underlying representation is a dense embedding refined by graph convolution.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Single tool/API (raw tool document level), not a distilled strategy, workflow, or trajectory. Dependency structure is captured at the representation level but the retrieved unit remains an individual tool.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Indirect: (1) a category-specific average training loss handles the severe class imbalance (dependencies are sparse) to avoid overfitting and reduce spurious dependency edges; (2) a 3-step validate-and-filter pipeline during pretraining-data construction discards tool pairs not meeting dependency criteria. There is no retrieved-context relevance evaluator or self-reflection at inference time; robustness against an inaccurate graph is limited by discriminator quality (acknowledged in Limitations).
memory_type: graph (a static tool dependency graph). No episodic/skill/workflow/latent agent memory.
write_back: false; the system does not store new experiences/cases/skills at deployment. The dependency graph and embeddings are built offline and frozen.
online_growth: false; the retrievable store does not grow at test time. Graphs and tool embeddings are induced offline.
write_back_trigger: never (no write-back / no online memory writes).
failure_experience_usage: N/A; no storage of success/failure trajectories. (The discriminator does learn from a 'no-dependency' negative class during training, but this is training-data balancing, not experiential failure memory.)
memory_evolution_update: N/A (static graph; no post-write mutation, dedup, pruning, or evolution).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval is similarity top-k over dependency-updated embeddings; it is not an RL/learned selection policy. The only learned component is the dependency discriminator (a classifier), and the graph convolution is parameter-free.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No; single-retriever / single-agent setting. The dependency graph is global over the tool set but is not described as shared across multiple agents or heterogeneous frameworks.
benchmarks: API-Bank (311 test samples across 3 levels) and ToolBench (I1 level subset; I2/I3 left to future work due to cross-category graph complexity). TDI300K (constructed) is used to train the dependency discriminator; the discriminator test set is derived from API-Bank tools.
baselines: Word-frequency retrievers: BM25 (Robertson et al. 2009), TF-IDF (Ramos et al. 2003). Text-embedding retrievers: Paraphrase MiniLM-L3-v2 / PMLM-L3-v2 (Reimers & Gurevych 2019, API-Bank's retriever) and ToolBench-IR (Qin et al. 2023, ToolBench's finetuned retriever). TGR is applied on top of the two embedding retrievers (PMLM-L3-v2+TGR, ToolBench-IR+TGR).
key_metrics: Recall@5, Recall@10, NDCG@5, NDCG@10, Pass Rate@5, Pass Rate@10 (pass@k = fraction of queries whose full ground-truth tool set is within top-k). Discriminator quality also reported via Precision/Recall/F1.
headline_result: TGR consistently improves base retrievers and reaches SOTA. Strongest single result: on API-Bank, ToolBench-IR+TGR raises Recall@10 from 0.790 to 0.878 and Pass Rate@10 from 0.624 to 0.788 over ToolBench-IR; on ToolBench-I1, ToolBench-IR+TGR raises Recall@5 0.709->0.742, NDCG@5 0.791->0.811, Pass Rate@10 0.690->0.730.
ablations: (1) Discriminator-built graph vs manually-annotated graph: +TGR-m outperforms +TGR-d on API-Bank for both encoders (e.g., ToolBench-IR+TGR-m Recall@10 0.893 vs +TGR-d 0.878; Pass Rate@10 0.817 vs 0.788), indicating graph quality bounds TGR and discriminator improvement is the key lever. (2) Graph density effect: recall increment (top-5) rises with tool dependency graph density across ToolBench categories, confirming dependencies drive gains and TGR is most effective for dependency-intensive tool sets. (3) Discriminator performance: Precision/Recall/F1 reported (valid 0.775/0.814/0.792; test 0.893/0.760/0.817). (4) Connected-node proportion analysis (API-Bank 0.420 vs ToolBench 0.824). (5) Case studies on API-Bank (GetUserToken prerequisite surfaced for DeleteAccount) and ToolBench (Get Today's Prediction surfaced).
evaluation_decoupling: Yes -- intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k, NDCG@k) and a completeness metric (Pass Rate@k) are reported; the discriminator is separately evaluated with Precision/Recall/F1 and graph connectivity/density analyses. Evaluation is at the retrieval level (not full agent task-success end-to-end), so retrieval quality is effectively decoupled from downstream LLM execution.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Process/retrieval-quality oriented: metrics score retrieval correctness (recall, ranking via NDCG, completeness via Pass Rate) rather than final agent task completion. No end-to-end agent outcome (e.g., final answer success) is the primary metric; Pass Rate captures whether the full required tool set is retrieved, an intermediate-process proxy.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency-conscious design: graph convolution is made parameter-free (GCN trainable weights removed) to accelerate online retrieval; tool embeddings are precomputed offline so online cost is a similarity ranking. Main cost concern is graph construction at O(N^2) pairwise dependency checks (noted as a limitation, mitigable by prior filtering rules). No latency/throughput numbers or API-cost figures are reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k top-k selection: top-5 and top-10 settings evaluated. No adaptive/precision-driven k and no explicit token-budget cap on injected tools is reported.
builds_on: ToolBench / ToolLLM and its ToolBench-IR retriever (Qin et al. 2023); API-Bank (Li et al. 2023); Gorilla (Patil et al. 2023) as dominant semantic-similarity tool-retrieval baselines; GCN graph convolution (Kipf & Welling 2017); BERT-base-uncased (Devlin et al. 2019) as discriminator backbone; CodeSearchNet (Husain et al. 2019, 1.78M functions) as pretraining-data source; Sentence-BERT / Paraphrase MiniLM-L3-v2 (Reimers & Gurevych 2019); evaluation protocol following Qu et al. 2024.
contrasts_with: Dominant semantic-similarity tool retrievers that treat each tool independently (ToolBench-IR/Qin et al. 2023, Gorilla/Patil et al. 2023, API-Bank/Li et al. 2023) and thus omit low-similarity prerequisite tools; word-frequency retrievers BM25 and TF-IDF. TGR explicitly contrasts by modeling inter-tool dependencies via a graph and graph convolution.
lineage: Group E (tool-use / tool retrieval). Sits in the tool-retrieval lineage that moves from independent semantic-similarity tool retrieval toward structure-aware retrieval, specifically introducing inter-tool dependency-graph modeling (graph-convolution-refined tool embeddings + a dependency identification dataset TDI300K) so prerequisite tools are recovered.
benchmark_construction_and_size: TDI300K (constructed dataset for tool dependency identification): format {<t_a,t_b>, y} with 3 classes (a->b, no-dependency, a<-b). Pretraining split is category-balanced 92,000 per class (~276K pairs), built via a 3-step LLM (gpt-3.5-turbo, 3 agents) pipeline over CodeSearchNet function implementations (extract tool document -> generate dependent tool document -> validate/filter). Finetuning split is manually constructed, category-imbalanced: 1,029 (a->b) / 33,365 (no-dependency) / 1,056 (a<-b), from open-source datasets/projects/libraries (incl. ToolBench training set, online shopping, OpenGL). Test set for the discriminator is manually annotated from API-Bank tools (60 / 500 / 60 per class). Answer verifiability: dependency labels are LLM-validated (pretraining) or human-annotated (finetuning/test). Discriminator difficulty signal: test F1 0.817.
